mainTopic: Abandoned babies (אסופי) and who is believed about a child's lineage or a sale
overview: The גמרא lists cases of babies found abandoned and decides whether each one is an אסופי, a foundling whose lineage is in doubt. If the parents showed care, by tending the baby or leaving him somewhere safe where he would be found, he is not an אסופי. If he was left somewhere dangerous, he is. רבא adds a famine-year rule, and the גמרא shows that it belongs to רב's teaching: parents are believed about an abandoned baby only while he is still in the marketplace, but in famine years they are believed even after he is taken in. רב חסדא then lists three people believed only right away: the parents of an אסופי, a midwife who never left the room, and a woman who checked herself immediately and so frees her friends from טומאה. A ברייתא adds that a midwife is believed about which baby is a כהן, a לוי, a נתין or a ממזר unless there is an עַרְעָר. The גמרא gives two answers about whether that challenge needs two witnesses or only one. Finally, a seller is believed about which of two buyers he sold to, but only while the item is still in his hands.

steps.title: Signs of care on the baby's body
steps.stepSummary: A baby found with signs that someone cared for him (circumcised, limbs set, oiled, eye salve, healing knots, a note, an amulet) is not an אסופי.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A baby found circumcised] is not considered an אסופי. If his limbs were set, he is not considered an אסופי. If he was rubbed with oil, his eyes smeared with salve, healing knots (charms) put on him, a note hung on him, or an amulet hung on him, he is not considered an אסופי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a list of signs that show the baby's parents cared for him, and rules that such a baby is not an אסופי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item shows effort spent on the baby after birth. Parents who abandon a child because of a lineage problem would not bother with these things. So we assume the parents gave him up for some other reason, and his lineage is not in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A foundling: a baby found abandoned whose parents are unknown, so his lineage is in doubt
He does not have the status of
His limbs were set or straightened (care given to a newborn)
Eye salve
An amulet

steps.confusionAlert: Not being an אסופי does not mean we know who the parents are. It only means we do not suspect that he was abandoned because of a lineage problem.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Visible signs of care on the baby remove the status of אסופי.

steps.title: A baby hanging from a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: If a wild animal can reach the baby, he is an אסופי. If it cannot, he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baby hung on palm trees: if an animal can reach him, he is an אסופי. If not, he is not an אסופי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from signs on the baby's body to the place where he was left, starting with a palm tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the test is whether the spot protected the baby. If he was hung out of animals' reach, the parents made sure he would survive, so he is not an אסופי. If animals could get to him, the parents did not care whether he lived, so he is an אסופי.

A wild animal
He has the status of
If not

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from signs on the baby to the safety of the spot where he was left.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Left within reach of animals: אסופי. Left out of their reach: not אסופי.

steps.title: A baby found in a thicket near a town
steps.stepSummary: A baby in a thicket near a town is an אסופי, and otherwise he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A thicket near a town: he is an אסופי. If not, he is not an אסופי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a ruling for a baby left in a thicket, which depends on whether the thicket is near a town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is still whether the spot shows the parents cared for the baby's survival. Near a town he is an אסופי, and elsewhere he is not. רש״י explains why: a tree near a town was thought to be a haunt of harmful spirits, so leaving the baby there shows no concern for his life.

keyTerms.meaning: A thicket or clump of bushes
Close to a town

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this case up with the next one (the synagogue). In this text the two rulings run in opposite directions, so read each one carefully.

phrases.english: A thicket near a town:
phrases.notes: זרדתא is a kind of tree. A tree near a town was thought to be a dangerous spot, as רש״י explains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another location case in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As printed: a thicket near a town means אסופי, otherwise not.

steps.title: A baby found in a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: A synagogue near town where many people are found means the baby is not an אסופי. Otherwise he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: A synagogue near a town, where many people are often found: he is not an אסופי. If not, he is an אסופי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules on a baby left in a בית כנסת. It depends on whether the place is near town and busy with people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving a baby in a busy synagogue means the parents wanted someone to find him and take care of him quickly. That shows concern, so he is not an אסופי. An empty or far-off synagogue gives no such protection, so he is an אסופי.

keyTerms.meaning: A synagogue
Many people are often found there

phrases.english: A synagogue near a town

he is not considered a foundling;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֲסוּפִי.
phrases.english: and if not, he is considered a foundling.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא סְמִיכְתָּא לְמָתָא וּשְׁכִיחִי בֵּיהּ רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another location case. Here the factor is a busy place where the baby will be found.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A busy synagogue near town: not אסופי. Otherwise: אסופי.

steps.title: אמימר's cases: a pit of date pits, a river, and the public road
steps.stepSummary: אמימר adds more locations. A pit of date pits, the riverside and the middle of the רשות הרבים mean אסופי. The middle of the river and the sides of the רשות הרבים mean not אסופי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: this pit of date pits means he is an אסופי. The fast-flowing middle of a river means he is not an אסופי. The riverbanks mean he is an אסופי. The sides of the public area mean he is not an אסופי. The public area itself means he is an אסופי.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר adds his own list of places where a baby might be found and says which ones make him an אסופי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same test applies. In the middle of the river, boats pass and someone will find him, so he is not an אסופי. On the sides of a public area he is safe from being trampled, so again he is not. A feeding pit, the riverbank, or the middle of a busy road are dangerous places, so a baby left there is an אסופי.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who adds rulings here
A pit where date pits are thrown for animal feed
The fast-flowing middle part of a river
The sides or banks (of the river)
A public area, where many people walk

steps.whatToRemember: Every case on this list asks one question: did the parents show they cared whether the baby lived? Care shown on his body or in a safe, findable spot means he is not an אסופי. A dangerous spot means he is an אסופי.
steps.whyThisMatters: An אסופי's lineage is in doubt, which limits whom he may marry. These rules decide whether a found child can marry freely.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
This pit of date pits:
he is considered a foundling.
The fast-flowing middle of a river:
he is not considered a foundling.
The sides of the river:
he is considered a foundling.
The sides of a public area:
he is not considered a foundling.
The public area itself:
he is considered a foundling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new speaker adds more location cases using the same test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dangerous spots (feeding pit, riverbank, middle of a public road) mean אסופי. Spots where he is safe or will be found (middle of a busy river, sides of a public road) mean not אסופי.

steps.title: רבא: In famine years there is no foundling status
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that in famine years a found baby is not treated as an אסופי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In famine years, a found baby does not have the status of an אסופי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new rule: in years of famine, an abandoned baby does not get the status of an אסופי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a famine, even parents with good lineage may abandon a baby because they cannot feed him. So abandoning him does not show that his lineage is flawed. רבא does not say which earlier case he means, and the גמרא will now try to work that out.

keyTerms.meaning: Years of famine
He does not have the status of a foundling
An אמורא who often adds rulings to a סוגיא

phrases.english: Rava said:
And in famine years,
he is not subject to the status of a foundling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a famine-year exception to the list of foundling locations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In famine years, a found baby is not an אסופי.

steps.title: Which case is רבא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier case רבא's famine rule refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of רבא, which case does it refer to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבא's rule belongs. This sets up the next steps, which will test different possible cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule like 'in famine years' only makes sense when it is attached to a specific case. The גמרא wants to know which ruling it changes.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? (which case does it refer to)

phrases.english: This statement of Rava, to which case does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבא's ruling is attached to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier case רבא's famine exception changes.

steps.title: It cannot be the middle of the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבא means a baby left in the middle of the רשות הרבים, because a famine would not make a mother put her baby where he could be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the public domain: just because it is a famine year, would she kill him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, the baby found in the middle of the רשות הרבים, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving a baby in the middle of the רשות הרבים puts him in danger of being trampled, so that is still a sign he was thrown away. A famine may push a mother to give up her baby, but not to put him in danger of death. So the famine changes nothing in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the גמרא offers a possibility to test it)
She kills him

phrases.english: If we say it refers to the public domain,
phrases.notes: He means אמימר's case from Step 5: a baby in the middle of the public domain is an אסופי.

phrases.english: just because they are famine years,
would she kill him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible case for רבא's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבא refers to the middle of the רשות הרבים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A famine does not explain putting a baby in a deadly spot, so that is still a sign of a thrown-away child.

steps.title: It cannot be the sides of the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבא means the sides of the רשות הרבים, because a baby left there is not an אסופי even without a famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it refers to the sides of the public domain, why mention famine years specifically? Even without famine years he is not an אסופי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, the sides of the רשות הרבים, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר already ruled that a baby at the sides of the רשות הרבים is not an אסופי, because he was put in a safe place. If so, adding 'in famine years' would teach nothing new, so רבא cannot mean that case.

keyTerms.meaning: The sides of the public domain
Why specifically this? (why mention this detail?)

phrases.english: Rather, if it refers to the sides of the public domain,
why specifically famine years?
Even without famine years!
phrases.notes: In Step 5, אמימר already said a baby at the sides is not an אסופי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the second possible case for רבא's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבא refers to the sides of the רשות הרבים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That baby is already not an אסופי, so the famine detail would add nothing.

steps.title: רבא's rule belongs to רב's ruling about parents' credibility
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule was said about רב's teaching: parents are believed about an abandoned baby while he is in the marketplace, but not after he has been taken from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא's statement was said about what רב taught: As long as the baby is in the marketplace, his father and mother are believed about him. Once he has been taken from the marketplace, they are no longer believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real setting for רבא's rule. It is a teaching of רב, passed down through several rabbis, about when parents can claim an abandoned baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic: not where the baby was found, but whether parents who later say 'he is ours' are believed. רב draws the line at the moment the baby is taken from the marketplace. רבא's famine rule will soften that line.

keyTerms.meaning: Marketplace
They are believed about him
He was collected (taken in)
When it was said (it was said about this)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Steps 1-5. Those asked whether the baby is an אסופי. Here the question is whether the parents' later claim is believed.

phrases.english: Rather, when Rava's statement was said,

As long as he is in the marketplace,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both options were rejected, gives the correct setting for רבא's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא's rule refers to רב's ruling that parents lose credibility once the baby is taken from the marketplace.

steps.title: Why aren't the parents believed after the baby is taken in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why parents lose credibility once the baby is taken in. This sets up רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first it seems odd. The parents are saying the same thing before and after, so why should the moment the baby is taken in make a difference?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why being taken from the marketplace makes the parents no longer believed.

steps.title: Because he is already known as a foundling
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that once the baby is taken in, he is publicly known as an אסופי, and the parents cannot undo that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because the name 'foundling' has already gone out about him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason: once the baby is taken in, everyone already knows him as an אסופי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the baby is still lying in the marketplace, his status is not yet settled. Once he is taken in, people already speak of him as an אסופי, and a later claim by the parents is not enough to remove that status.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
A name (reputation) went out about him

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since there has already gone out about him
the name of a foundling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הוֹאִיל וְיָצָא עָלָיו שֵׁם אֲסוּפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The baby is already publicly known as an אסופי, so the parents cannot change his status.

steps.title: In famine years the parents are believed even after he is taken in
steps.stepSummary: רבא's famine rule is now in its proper place: in famine years, the parents are believed even after the baby has been taken from the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: In famine years, even though he was taken in from the marketplace, his father and mother are believed about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now repeats רבא's famine rule in its proper setting. In a famine, parents are believed even after the baby has been taken in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a famine, even parents with good lineage abandon babies because they cannot feed them. So the name 'foundling' does not suggest flawed lineage, and the parents' claim is accepted. This is the same rule as Step 6, now understood correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though

steps.whatToRemember: רב: parents are believed about an abandoned baby only while he is still in the marketplace, because once he is taken in he is known as an אסופי. רבא: in famine years, the parents are believed even after that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the meaning of רבא's short line from Step 6: in famine years, the parents are still believed.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
phrases.notes: This is the same famine rule from Step 6, now said in its proper setting.

phrases.english: And in famine years,

his father and mother are believed about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: וּבִשְׁנֵי רְעָבוֹן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱסַף מִן הַשּׁוּק

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In famine years, parents are believed about an abandoned baby even after he has been taken from the marketplace.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Three who are believed immediately
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא lists three people who are believed if they speak right away: the parents of an אסופי, a midwife, and a woman who exempts her friends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Three are believed if they speak immediately. They are: about a foundling, a midwife, and a woman who exempts her friends.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא starts a new teaching. He lists three cases where someone is believed only if they speak right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the person's word counts only at first, before the situation could change: before the baby is taken in, before the midwife leaves, before time passes after the blood is found. The first case connects to what we just learned: parents are believed about an אסופי if they speak before he is taken in. The other two cases are only named here, and the next steps explain them.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately, right away
Midwife
A woman who exempts her friends
An אמורא who teaches this list

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Three are believed immediately;
these are they: a foundling,
a midwife, and one who exempts her friends.
phrases.notes: Here חיה means a midwife, not the wild animal from Step 2.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שְׁלֹשָׁה נֶאֱמָנִים לְאַלְתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching, connected through the idea that parents of an אסופי are believed only at first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In three cases, someone is believed only if they speak right away: about an אסופי, a midwife, and a woman who exempts her friends.

steps.title: The foundling case is the one already discussed
steps.stepSummary: The first item on רב חסדא's list, the parents of an אסופי, is the case the גמרא has already explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'foundling' case is what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining each item in רב חסדא's list of three. For the first one, it simply points back to the earlier discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parents of an אסופי are believed while the baby is still in the marketplace, before he is taken in. That early window is the 'right away' רב חסדא meant, so nothing new needs to be said. רבא's famine rule is an extra exception and is not part of this 'right away' idea.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we already said

phrases.english: A foundling — that is what we already said.
phrases.notes: This points back to steps 10-13: the parents are believed while the baby is still in the marketplace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first item in רב חסדא's list from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the אסופי case in רב חסדא's list?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the case discussed earlier: the parents are believed while the baby is in the marketplace.

steps.title: The midwife is believed about which twin came out first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a midwife is believed about the order of birth, but only if she did not leave the room and come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The midwife case is from a ברייתא: A midwife is believed to say 'this one came out first and this one came out second.' When is that true? When she did not leave and come back. If she left and came back, she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second item on רב חסדא's list, the midwife, by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The midwife's word decides which twin is the בכור. She is believed only if she stayed the whole time. Once she leaves and returns, the babies could have been switched, so her word is no longer 'right away.'

keyTerms.meaning: A midwife
As was taught in a ברייתא
She is believed
When is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)

phrases.english: A midwife — as it was taught:

phrases.notes: This is about twins. The one born first is the בכור, the firstborn.

phrases.english: and this one came out second.

When she did not go out and come back,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second item on רב חסדא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the midwife case in רב חסדא's list?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A midwife is believed about the birth order of twins, as long as she never left the room.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: she must have stayed fixed in her place
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the midwife is believed only if she stayed steadily in her spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: If she stayed firmly in her place, she is believed. If not, she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives his own version of the limit on the midwife's believability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion only asks whether she left the room. רבי אליעזר's wording, 'stayed firmly in her place,' sounds stricter. The גמרא will now ask what the real difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: She stayed firmly in her place
And if not

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא about when the midwife is believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The midwife is believed only if she stayed steadily in her place.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר's view differs from the first opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two opinions. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions seem to require the midwife to stay with the babies. The גמרא wants a case where they would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.title: The difference: she turned her face away
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions disagree when the midwife stayed in the room but turned her face away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a case where she turned her face away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions disagree about a midwife who stayed in the room but looked away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion she is still believed, because she never left. According to רבי אליעזר, even turning her face means she was not watching steadily, so she is not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
She turned her face away

phrases.english: The difference between them is where she turned her face away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If she turned her face away but stayed in the room, the first opinion still believes her and רבי אליעזר does not.

steps.title: What is 'she exempts her friends'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the third case on רב חסדא's list means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'she exempts her friends'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the third item on רב חסדא's list and asks what it refers to. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first two items, this phrase is unclear on its own: exempts her friends from what? The גמרא will answer with a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: She exempts (frees) her friends
What is it?

phrases.english: She who exempts her friends, what is that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third item on רב חסדא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does 'she exempts her friends' refer to?

steps.title: Three women in one bed and blood is found
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that if blood is found under one of three women in a bed, all are טמאות. If one checks and finds herself טמאה, the others are טהורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Three women were sleeping in one bed, and blood was found under one of them. All of them are טמאות. If one of them checked herself and found that she is טמאה, she is טמאה and all the others are טהורות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a משנה: one woman's check can free the other women from טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody knows whose blood it is, all three are first treated as נדות. When one woman checks and finds that she is bleeding, we assume the blood came from her. That clears her friends.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Ritually impure (here, as נדות)
She checked (examined) herself
Ritually pure

phrases.english: As we learned: three women
who were sleeping in one bed
and blood was found under one of them —
they are all impure.
If one of them checked herself and was found impure —
she is impure, and all the others are pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים שֶׁהָיוּ יְשֵׁנוֹת בְּמִטָּה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is the משנה where one woman's check, showing she is טמאה, makes her friends טהורות.

steps.title: רב חסדא: only if she checked right away
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the משנה: the check frees the others only if it was done within the short time of a שיעור וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is only when she checked herself within the time of a שיעור וסת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a condition to the משנה: the woman must have checked herself immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she checked later, her bleeding might have started only after the blood was found, so it proves nothing about the earlier blood. This is exactly why רב חסדא listed her among people believed only 'right away.'

keyTerms.meaning: Within the very short time it takes for bleeding to begin, meaning immediately

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the common thread of all three cases: each person's word counts only when given right away, before things could have changed.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
When she checked herself within the time of a שיעור וסת.
phrases.notes: A שיעור וסת is a very short amount of time, so she checked right after the blood was found.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שֶׁבָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ כְּשִׁיעוּר וֶוסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The woman's check frees her friends only if she did it immediately.

steps.title: A midwife is believed about which baby belongs to which mother
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a midwife is believed to say which baby is a כהן, a לוי, a נתין or a ממזר, unless someone has raised a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A midwife is believed to say 'this one is a כהן and this one is a לוי, this one is a נתין and this one is a ממזר.' When is that true? When no challenge was raised against her. If a challenge was raised, she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about a midwife's believability, this time about which baby was born to which mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When several babies are born together, the midwife's word decides each baby's lineage. A challenge (ערער) against her takes that away. Without a challenge she is believed, even when her word makes a baby a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
A descendant of the גבעונים, who may not marry into the community
A child born from a forbidden relationship
A challenge or objection raised against someone's claim

steps.whatToRemember: All three people on רב חסדא's list are believed only in a 'right away' window: parents while the baby is still in the marketplace, a midwife who never left, and a woman who checked immediately. A midwife is also believed about lineage, unless someone challenges her.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A midwife is believed to say:
this one is a priest and this one is a Levite,
phrases.notes: Several women gave birth together, and she is saying which baby belongs to which mother.

phrases.english: this one is a Gibeonite and this one is a mamzer.
When is this said?
When no challenge was raised about it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קָרָא עָלֶיהָ עַרְעָר – אֵינָהּ נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: but if a challenge was raised about it, she is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא about the midwife, widening her believability from birth order to lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A midwife is believed about the lineage of each baby unless a challenge was raised against her.

steps.title: What counts as a challenge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of עַרְעָר the ברייתא means when it says the midwife is believed unless there is a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: A challenge of what kind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last words of the ברייתא, 'unless there is a challenge,' and asks what that challenge is. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the midwife loses her believability when there is an עַרְעָר. It did not say how many witnesses that takes. The גמרא wants to know whether one witness is enough or two are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A challenge or objection, here witnesses who say the midwife is wrong
Of what kind?

phrases.english: A challenge of what kind?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא's words 'unless someone has raised a challenge' from step 23.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the ברייתא quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the עַרְעָר that cancels the midwife's believability is one witness or two.

steps.title: One witness cannot be meant, because of רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the idea that the challenge is one witness, then rejects it using רבי יוחנן's rule that an עַרְעָר needs at least two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a challenge by one witness, that is a problem, because רבי יוחנן said: there is no challenge with fewer than two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible answer, that one witness is enough, and pushes it away with a known rule from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן taught that an objection only counts when it comes from two witnesses. So the ברייתא cannot mean that one witness is enough to cancel the midwife's word. This shuts out the first option.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the גמרא tests an option it is about to reject)
A challenge by one witness
There is no challenge with fewer than two witnesses

phrases.english: If you say it means a challenge by one witness,
but didn't רבי יוחנן say:
There is no challenge with fewer than two!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא עַרְעָר חַד, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that one witness is enough to make an עַרְעָר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's rule says an objection needs at least two witnesses, so one witness cannot count.

steps.title: The challenge means two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא means a challenge by two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a challenge by two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: Since one witness was ruled out, the גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רבי יוחנן's rule. The result is that the midwife loses her believability only when two witnesses argue with her. If only one witness argues, she is still believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the accepted option)
A challenge by two witnesses

phrases.english: Rather, it means a challenge by two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after step 25 rejected the one-witness reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עַרְעָר in the ברייתא is two witnesses.

steps.title: Second answer: even one witness counts here
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the ברייתא really can mean one witness, because רבי יוחנן's rule only applies where there is a חזקה דכשרות, and a newborn baby has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really, I can tell you it means a challenge by one witness. When רבי יוחנן said there is no challenge with fewer than two, that applies only where there is a חזקה דכשרות. Where there is no חזקה דכשרות, even one witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer the question from step 24. It keeps the one-witness reading and narrows רבי יוחנן's rule so it does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's 'two witnesses' rule protects someone who already has a חזקה דכשרות, meaning he is already assumed to be fine. A newborn has no such status yet, so there is nothing to protect. That is why one witness is enough to cancel the midwife's word.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Really, actually (keeps the option that was pushed away)
A standing assumption that a person is valid and of proper lineage
This applies only (limits a rule)
Is believed

steps.confusionAlert: This second answer does not argue with רבי יוחנן. It agrees with his rule but limits it to cases where there is a חזקה דכשרות to protect.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: (1) the challenge is two witnesses, as רבי יוחנן says; (2) the challenge can be one witness, because a newborn has no חזקה דכשרות, and רבי יוחנן's rule only protects someone who has one.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Really, I can tell you it means a challenge by one witness.
And when רבי יוחנן said
there is no challenge with fewer than two,
that applies only where
there is a standing assumption of validity,
but where there is no standing assumption of validity,
even one witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ עַרְעָר חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 24. It saves the one-witness reading that step 25 rejected by limiting רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עַרְעָר can be one witness, since רבי יוחנן's rule only applies when a חזקה דכשרות exists.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's rule seemed to require two witnesses for every objection.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only protects a person with a חזקה דכשרות. A newborn has none, so one witness is enough.

steps.title: The seller is believed about who bought from him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a similar case: a seller is believed to say which of two buyers he really sold to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner of an item for sale is believed to say: I sold it to this one, and I did not sell it to that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new case that works like the midwife: a seller is believed when two people each claim they bought his item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the midwife is believed about which baby is which, the seller is believed about which person is the real buyer. He is the one who knows, and the item is still under his control.

keyTerms.meaning: Is believed
The owner of an item being sold, the seller
I sold

phrases.english: The owner of an item for sale is believed to say:
I sold it to this one, and I did not sell it to that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from step 23 and quotes its next, parallel ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller is believed to say which of two claimants he sold the item to.

steps.title: Only while the item is still in his hands
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the seller's believability: it works only while the item is still with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When the item is still in his possession. But if the item is not in his possession, he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets a limit on the rule from step 28.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the seller still holds the item, he controls it, so his word decides who gets it. Once the item has left his hands, he is just an outside person with no special power. Then he is not believed any more than a single witness.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
His item for sale is in his hand, still in his possession

steps.whatToRemember: The seller is believed about who bought from him only while the item is still in his hands.

phrases.english: When is this said?
When the item is still in his possession,
but if the item is not in his possession,
he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the seller's believability from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller is believed only while the item is in his possession; otherwise he is not believed.
